The center will reimburse $0.625/mile traveled as per university recommendations.

300 (miles) x $0.625/mile = $187.50

# Student Travel Grant
The board of the AETE recognizes that presenting research at conferences is vital aspect of a student’s professional, educational and research development. Furthermore, student involvement in our
conferences is fundamental to further develop our research community.
AETE Student Travel Grant will make a partial financial contribution to student presenters attending our annual international conference, subject to available funds. The number of available
grants will be announced on**February 15th**each year. If awarded, the student will receive the bursary after the conference using electronic money transfer. The precise
value will be specified, but up to a**maximum of 250€ per awardee**. The award can be used to cover costs associated with the travel, the hotel and the registration for our
AETE conference.

## Call for Student Travel Award Applications
#### **Description**
KDD is a premier conference that brings together researchers and practitioners from data mining, knowledge discovery, data analytics, and big data. Students, who might otherwise be unable to participate, now have the opportunity to attend sessions, tutorials, and workshops, meet other students and researchers from industry and academia, and take advantage of everything KDD’26 has to offer!
KDD’26 will offer travel awards to full-time student attendees. The purpose of the travel grants is to encourage students to participate in the exciting technical and other career enhancement programs at KDD.
The maximum amount of support provided to each grantee as the number of awards is subject to the availability of funds by the sponsors. The award is intended to partially cover the grantee’s expenses. Conference registration will be waived for student travel award grantees. The allocation of the grants will be based on need and acceptance of the student’s publication at KDD’26.
All full-time undergraduate and graduate students interested in data mining or machine learning-related research are encouraged to apply. There is no need to have a paper accepted at the conference to apply.

The AnitaB.org Kamala Scholars Program empowers the next generation of innovators by providing resources, mentorship, and access to Grace Hopper Celebration.

## About the Kamala Scholars Program
The Kamala Scholars Program is a year-long opportunity made possible through the generosity of an anonymous donor, in honor of a family member, and is dedicated to opening doors and creating pathways for 3rd- and 4th-year undergraduate students pursuing technical computing fields. AnitaB.org offers many opportunities to elevate the full diaspora of our community. This particular scholarship is focused exclusively on Black and Latine students, in alignment with the donor’s wishes. Each year, we welcome 100 students into the program.
